products.name: Autel Robotics EVO Lite 640T Thermal Drone, Basic Combo (640 × 512 thermal, 40-minute flight)
products.warranty: 1 year from Autelpilot, starting the day after delivery; the store advertises a free 1-year extension after registration
products.summary: The lowest-priced full 640 × 512 thermal drone we found sold new in the US, with up to 40 minutes of flight and a 12 km video link.
products.fit: Hunters who want to find their own deer without paying about $7,100 for a DJI Matrice 4T.
caveats: Obstacle sensors cover only the front, rear and bottom, not the sides.
Zoom is digital only, with no laser rangefinder, so it is harder to confirm a deer from far away than with the Matrice 4T.
No spotlight or strobe is listed for it; use the EVO II Dual 640T V3 Enterprise Bundle for night work with lights.
Autel has been on the FCC Covered List since December 22, 2025. Firmware updates are allowed through at least January 1, 2029, but future sales and parts supply are uncertain.

products.summary: A 640 × 512 thermal drone with 360° obstacle sensing that comes with a spotlight, a strobe and a speaker, for night searches in timber.
products.fit: Hunters and landowners who search at night and want a light to confirm the deer and a strobe for Part 107 night flights.
caveats: In a 2026 r/drones thread on this model, 2 of 3 replies reported radio connection errors or weak-GPS warnings after a July 2024 firmware update.

notes: Brand: Autelpilot (autelpilot.com) is a US Shopify dealer for Autel Robotics drones. It advertises a US warehouse, free US shipping, 30-day money back and a 1-year warranty, plus a free 1-year extension after registration (homepage, 2026-11-10). Query choice: 'best thermal drone for deer recovery'. The current top results are mostly thin affiliate listicles (pwice, sloweather, lensespro, aerovisiondrones) and dealer pages. Pain points, with how often each came up: (1) state legality, in 5 sources (American Hunter, Outdoor Life, Bowhunting.com and 2 search summaries); (2) cost, in 4 (Bowhunting.com says 'well into five figures', Outdoor Life gives service fees, plus listicles); (3) the FCC Covered List, the PS Docket 26-189 proposal and tariffs, in 6+ articles (DroneDJ, CineD, DroneBundle x2, DroneLife, law-firm alerts); (4) Autel radio, GNSS and firmware problems, 4 mentions (2 of 3 replies in a 2026 r/drones thread, a 2023 autelpilots.com 'legal demand' thread, and a 'firmware check failed' thread); (5) Autelpilot store support on Trustpilot: 3.7 from 174 reviews, 23% one-star, of the 6 visible low reviews about 4 cite email-only support, 3 refunds/chargebacks and 2 non-delivery; (6) canopy slowing heat detection, 2 sources (American Hunter, Outdoor Life); (7) Matrice 4T limits, 2 sources: no IP rating, 104 °F max and -10 °C floor (r/drones and DroneBundle). Segment winners: pro recovery services go to the DJI Matrice 4T (American Hunter: Covert Drones' most-used model, Drone Deer Recovery ranks 4T/4TD about tied). Hunters buying for their own use on a budget go to the Autel EVO Lite 640T Basic Combo at $3,359, the lowest-priced new 640 × 512 thermal drone I found. Night recovery with lights and 360° sensing goes to the EVO II Dual 640T V3 Enterprise Bundle at $5,299. Occasional users should hire a service. The Matrice 4T is not linked: there is no Amazon record per the temporary rule, and DJI does not sell it direct. Prices verified today with storecheck search on autelpilot.com: Lite 640T Basic $3,359 and Plus $3,879, EVO II 640T V3 Rugged $4,799 and Enterprise $5,299, all available. The store's compare_at for the Lite 640T is LOWER than the price ($3,299 vs $3,359, and $3,829 vs $3,879 on the Plus), so I left out list_price. storecheck 'product' and WebFetch of the product pages returned HTTP 429 all session, so variants and box contents were not read. UNVERIFIED, kept off the page: Lite 640T Basic Combo battery count and controller (retailer snippets say Smart Controller SE V2 and one battery); Lite 640T 9.1 mm thermal lens, ≤50 mK, IP43 and 866 g (reseller snippets only); EVO II 640T V3 visible-camera megapixels (the store text says 12 MP, other listings say 48/50 MP); the Matrice 4T price today (the page uses the DroneBundle Sept 2026 dealer survey of $7,079–$7,199 for a kit; snippets showed $6,999–$7,849); Tennessee and Missouri legalizing drone recovery (snippets only). The Michigan ban status is as of 2024. FCC PS Docket 26-189 had no final order as of October 2026 (Drone Authority / DroneBundle); I found nothing newer. Codes: no network codes were given, and no code is printed on the Autelpilot homepage, only an '11.11 Mega Sale, save up to $300' banner and a newsletter 'welcome gift' with no code shown.
